title: Install a library — Running a library
sub: You leave with the engine installed, a repository set up, every check passing, and its pages in your browser.
defn: PIN — definition of record A library's pin is two records of what it was checked against: the engine version in kit.json (the "ckit" key), which ckit check compares with the engine running it, and a hash of the copied kit/ in kit/PIN, which make kit-verify recomputes. Either mismatch fails, and neither changes except on purpose.

title: Running a library
sub: Five chapters that take a repository from nothing to a gated, reviewable library of pages, for whoever sets one up and keeps it in order, human or agent.

title: Annotation
sub: Definition of record. A reader's comment on a page, kept in a file beside it, so the reader and the agent who answers never need to be there at the same time.
defn: ANNOTATION — definition of record An annotation is a thread on a page: a comment on a quoted passage, or on the whole page, with its replies. It is stored in a sidecar, a committed file beside the page, and anchored by the quoted text and a little of the text around it, not by the page's markup. It is one of two kinds. title: Chronicle
sub: Definition of record. The timeline of a repository, generated from its record, so that nobody writes history twice.
defn: CHRONICLE — definition of record The chronicle is a timeline generated from the record. Every heading in a record file that opens with a date becomes an event; a bracketed tag after the date names the event's kind, and an untagged heading is a plain entry. title: Extension point
sub: Definition of record. A declared place where a repository adds to the engine without changing it, and why each one is checked.
defn: EXTENSION POINT — definition of record An extension point is one of the ten keys in kit.json through which a repository, or a layer installed into it, adds to what the engine does without changing the engine: genres, checks, generators, chronicle.extractors, shell_pages, links, refs, theme, classes and indices. title: Gate
sub: Definition of record. The one command that decides whether a library may land, and why it reports instead of repairing.
defn: GATE — definition of record The gate is the command ckit check, run before anything lands. It fails when the engine version the repository pins differs from the engine running, when the shell is missing, when a kit.json declaration does not hold, when a generated index differs from what the content would generate, when a page breaks its form or its genre's checks, when an open annotation has lost

title: Genre
sub: Definition of record. The kind of page a page is: where it lives decides how it is built, how it reads, and what the gate checks on it.
defn: GENRE — definition of record A genre is the kind of page a page is, decided by where the page lives in the content tree. It carries a structure (a directory, a layout and a skeleton to start from), a voice (a register, an assumed reader and the moves that are forbidden) and the checks the gate runs on every page of that kind. A page that lives under no genre is an error, not a default.

title: Record
sub: Definition of record. The markdown files that say how the work got where it is, kept apart from the pages that say where it is now.
defn: RECORD — definition of record The record is the set of markdown files a repository declares in kit.json under record (a field log, a decision log, a changelog): files that grow by appending and say how the work got where it is. The shell renders each one read-only at /shell/record.html?p=<path> and lists it in the sidebar. Pages under the content directory say where the work stands, and link into

title: Skeleton
sub: Definition of record. The file a page of a genre starts from, so that it starts inside the contract.
defn: SKELETON — definition of record A skeleton is the starting file of a genre: an HTML page that already links the shell, opens with a one-line lede, holds the genre's parts in their order, and says in placeholder prose what goes in each. ckit new <genre> <slug> copies it to the path the genre names, and the author replaces every placeholder.

title: Why hand-authored HTML
sub: Why content-kit pages are written as HTML by whoever writes them, served exactly as written, with no markdown source and no build, and what that costs.
defn: THE POSITION A page is one HTML file, written directly by its author (usually an agent) against one shared shell of styles and scripts, and served byte for byte as it was written. There is no source format behind it, no generator in front of it, and so no second version of it anywhere.

title: The design law
sub: A layer without a mechanical check is a suggestion; every check ships with a fixture designed to break it.

title: The placement rule
sub: Mechanisms below, conventions above: if it makes sense in a code repository's docs, it belongs in content-kit; if it only makes sense in a lab or a personal library, it belongs in a layer.

title: Twins drift
sub: A document kept in two formats is two documents, and they drift apart.
